correctness.rationale: Bang--Zsigmondy primitive divisors applied to the p-part force a prime s with ord_s(p)=k(b+1) and s|(a+1). A primitive divisor from the 2-part then must equal p, forcing a+1|p-1 and hence ord_s(p)=1, a contradiction. The sole base-2 Zsigmondy exception is separately eliminated.

originality.rationale: The checked literature records only weaker necessary congruence conditions for hypothetical proper k-harmonic numbers 2^a p^b. Searches did not locate complete nonexistence for this support pattern. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk because the full 1998 Cohen--Deng paper was not directly inspected.

value.rationale: The theorem removes the entire even two-distinct-prime search space for every k>=2 and all exponents, sharpening earlier congruence restrictions into a uniform structural obstruction.
